A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perturb-and-Merge research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning accuracy results, perturbation ablations, loss-landscape analyses, and resource measurements in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds comparator evaluations, coefficient-granularity experiments, and an online Fisher variant.

M1.justification: The principal perturbation-and-merging procedure remains unchanged. Appendix B.5 adds LoRA-online P&M, which maintains a running-average Fisher representation instead of separate per-task Fishers. A per-module merging-coefficient variant is also evaluated, while the default remains a global coefficient.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-classification datasets and domains: ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, DomainNet/DN*, CIFAR100, and CUB200. The added CIFAR100 20-task experiment changes the partition of existing coverage, not the represented dataset or task family.

E2.justification: v4 substantially broadens the evaluated alternatives: Table 9 adds O-LoRA, DualP-PGP, and C-Prompt, while Table 11 adds LoRA-EWC. These methods were absent from v1's reported comparisons. The original continual-learning and model-merging comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 20-task CIFAR100 partition and controlled comparisons of global versus per-module coefficients and separate versus averaged Fishers. Existing experiments retain their stated backbone, LoRA rank, learning rates, batch size, epoch budgets, and Acc/AAA metrics.

E4.justification: New studies test two previously unexamined design questions: whether a global merging coefficient is sufficiently flexible (Table 6), and how fixed-size Fisher storage affects accuracy as task sequences lengthen (Table 10). These substantially extend the design and scalability analyses; the original perturbation, landscape, hyperparameter, and resource analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that means and standard deviations are reported over three runs, and the retained uncertainty-bearing tables are unchanged. New tables report point estimates, following an existing reporting practice. No new seed specification, confidence interval, significance test, or increased run count is documented.

E6.justification: All original numerical tables retain their values after matching relocations. Tables 6 and 9–11 add substantial results, including 85.45 Acc on CIFAR100 with 20 tasks and online P&M's 71.20 versus standard P&M's 76.37 on ImageNet-R with 20 tasks. Figure 3 also changes some plotted accuracies slightly. Table 9's new ImageNet-R 10-task value of 81.47 conflicts with the retained 79.95 in Table 2; it does not establish a comparable-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The closed-form coefficient and regularizer derivations, including Appendix A's proofs, remain substantively unchanged. However, Section 3.2 changes the stated approximation from Fisher approximately H to Fisher approximately -H while retaining H's definition as the loss Hessian, introducing a local mathematical inconsistency. Equation 17's module-insertion notation is principally a clarification.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces an unqualified analytical solution for the optimal coefficient with a closed-form solution 'under mild assumptions,' modestly narrowing that claim. The central merging, perturbation, efficiency, and state-of-the-art contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds a rationale that global scaling preserves task-vector structure and interprets similar per-module coefficients as supporting the global choice. Appendix B.5 explicitly discusses growing Fisher storage and attributes the online variant's longer-sequence degradation to accumulated approximation error. The original diagonal-Fisher optimality limitation remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository location and Algorithm 2 documenting Fisher accumulation, parameter masking, and normalization; Algorithm 1 now references it. Existing implementation and hardware details remain. The new pseudocode squares batch-average gradients, which does not match Equation 10's per-example estimator for multi-example batches, leaving an implementation inconsistency.

R1.justification: v4 adds PGP and C-Prompt citations and a focused explanation distinguishing its inference-time curvature use from EWC's training-time importance regularization. O-LoRA and EWC were already cited in v1; their additional bibliography entries do not represent newly introduced works. The main related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: Most introduction, related-work, method, and conclusion prose is retained. Additional benchmark discussion moves into the main text, Appendix B gains numbered subsections, and local explanations are added. Author and conference information changes, and an acknowledgment section is introduced.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially expanded and rearranged: v4 adds Tables 6 and 9–11 plus Algorithm 2, and moves v1's appendix Tables 5–6 into the main text as Tables 4–5. Figure 3 is redrawn with different typography, colors, and axis ticks. Figures 1–2 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful baseline comparisons, design analyses, an explicit memory tradeoff, and a code pointer. However, its new Table 9 conflicts with the retained ImageNet-R result, Algorithm 2 conflicts with Equation 10 for multi-example batches, and the revised Fisher-Hessian sign introduces a mathematical inconsistency. These additions improve the discussion while weakening consistency in results and implementation documentation. The PDFs do not resolve these conflicts, so a reliable net improvement in overall quality cannot be established.
